headline: Intelligence takes many forms—verbal, mathematical, spatial, musical, social, physical, and more
universal_truth: Smart isn't one thing; find the intelligence you have rather than lamenting one you don't
fun_facts: Howard Gardner identified at least 8 distinct types of intelligence
Einstein was average at school but exceptional at spatial-visual thinking
Emotional intelligence predicts success better than IQ in many careers
discussion_questions: What type of intelligence are you strongest in?
How does your intelligence type shape your approach to problems?
What intelligence have you undervalued in yourself or others?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A master musician might fail at math. A brilliant mathematician might be socially awkward. A natural leader might struggle to draw. Intelligence isn't one thing—it's many. Smart takes different forms.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Schools often measure one or two types of intelligence. But people are smart in many ways. Why does recognizing multiple intelligences matter?

options.text: Recognizing multiple intelligences reveals hidden strengths—you might be brilliant in ways that aren't measured or valued in typical contexts; find where your intelligence shines
options.response: Yes. If you only measure verbal and mathematical, you miss spatial, musical, kinesthetic, social, and more. Many people are brilliant in ways schools never measure. Find your type.
True, and recognizing specific types helps you deploy your particular strengths...

q1.title: Multiple Paths
q1.script: There are many paths to being smart—linguistic, logical, spatial, musical, bodily, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic. Each is real, valuable intelligence.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Multiple Paths"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Find Your Type
q2.script: Knowing your intelligence type helps you learn better, work smarter, and contribute where you're strongest. Leverage your actual intelligence, not the one you wish you had.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Value Others' Intelligence
q3.script: People are smart in different ways. The person who seems slow might be brilliant in areas you're blind to. Value diverse intelligences—in yourself and others.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Smart isn't one thing. Find the intelligence you have rather than lamenting one you don't. Leverage your particular brilliance.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 292. Tomorrow, we'll explore natural abilities and practice—talent. Until then, consider which intelligences you're strongest in.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Intelligence Profile - Where Are You Smart?
growTrack.activity: Consider the types of intelligence: verbal, logical, spatial, musical, bodily, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic. Where are you strongest? How can you leverage these strengths more deliberately?
